items.stem: A model keeps calling a 'search' tool when the user clearly wants to 'create_ticket'. The tools are named and typed correctly. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Improve the tool descriptions so each states precisely when it should and should not be used
options.rationale: Correct: descriptions are the model's main signal for tool selection; disambiguating them fixes mis-selection.
Removing a needed capability is not a general fix for selection errors.
Context size is unrelated to tool-selection clarity.

options.text: Return the search results as an image
options.rationale: Output format does not fix which tool is chosen.

items.explanation: Correct: descriptions are the model's main signal for tool selection; disambiguating them fixes mis-selection.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make tool arguments safer to execute? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Validate and type-check arguments before executing the tool
options.rationale: Correct: validation catches malformed or unsafe arguments.

options.text: Scope each tool to the least privilege it needs
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits the damage of a bad call.

options.text: Trust any arguments the model produces because it is usually right
options.rationale: Blind trust is exactly the unsafe practice to avoid.

options.text: Execute every tool with full administrator rights for convenience
options.rationale: Over-privileged tools magnify harm from mistakes.

items.explanation: Correct: validation catches malformed or unsafe arguments.

items.stem: What happens in function calling after the model emits a tool call?

options.text: The application parses the call, executes the function, and returns the result to the model for the next step
options.rationale: Correct: the model requests; the application executes and returns results.

options.text: The model directly runs the code inside itself
options.rationale: The model only requests a call; it does not execute code.
The result is normally fed back so the model can continue.
The result is returned to the model to use.

items.explanation: Correct: the model requests; the application executes and returns results.
